findings.text: follow-on: the manifest test_logs names census-actionable-2.log and its landing and notes cite it as the second-census evidence, but the file does not exist on disk. The probe command meant to write it passed the path as an argument (python - "$RUN/census-actionable-2.log") rather than redirecting stdout to it, and the probe script ignores that argument, so its records-to-import: 0 was printed to the terminal and never landed in the named log; a reader of test_logs cannot open the artifact the zero-to-import figure is attributed to.

follow-on: the dry run prints the store inventory (recognised records, non-records, duplicates, delivered reports) but no records-to-import count, because the actionable set (a record whose committed path is absent) is computed only inside _import_records on the --write path. The brief step-4 figure therefore cannot be read from the command it names; it rests on an ad-hoc probe of the script own functions. Exposing the actionable count on the dry-run path would let the census reproduce its headline number.
